On the right branch there is an inductive reactance labeled jX_L. On the bottom branch there is a capacitive reactance labeled -jX_C. The left side shows the applied voltage U across the two terminals. Thus the resistor, inductor, and capacitor are connected in series. Reasoning: For a series RLC circuit, impedances add directly: Z = R + jX_L - jX_C = R + j(X_L - X_C). Using phasor Ohm's law, U = I Z. method.method_draft: From the series path, assign the same current I to all elements. Express voltage drops as phasors: V_R = IR along the current axis, V_L = j I X_L, and V_C = -j I X_C. The supply voltage phasor is their sum, so its magnitude satisfies U = I sqrt(R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2). Rearranging yields I = U / sqrt(R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2).
